Let& $I = {∫}_{0}^{20\pi}\left(\left|\sin x\right| + \left|\cos x\right|\right)2dx$

We know that the period of~\left|\sin x\right| + \left|\cos x\right|$~is~$\dfrac{π}{2}$

i.e.~$I = 40{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\left(\sin x + \cos x\right)2dx$

$I = 40{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\left(1 + \sin 2x\right)dx$

$= 40{x - \dfrac{\cos 2x}{2}}_{0}^{\pi2} = 40 \left(\dfrac{π}{2} - \dfrac{cosπ}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 0}{2}\right)$

$I = 20 \left[\pi +2\right]$

$

questions.q: The integral $\mathop{∫}_{1}^{e}\left\{\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)2x - \left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)x\right\}lo{g}_{e}xdx$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{1}^{e}{\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x}{\log_{\mathrm{e}}x}_{} dx$

Let \left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)x = t$

Taking natural logarithm on both sides, we get

$x\text\ln\dfrac{x}{e} = \text\lnt$

$⇒ x \left(\text\lnx - 1\right) = \text\lnt . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

$x$ $t$
$1$ $1\left(\ln 1 - 1\right) = \ln t ⇒ t = $\dfrac{1}{e}
$e$ $e \left(lne - 1\right) = \ln t ⇒ t = 1$

Differentiating equation \left(i\right)$~on both~the sides, we get

$\text\lnx - 1 + $x \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)$dx = $\dfrac{1}{t}$dt$

\text{⇒ln}$xdx = $\dfrac{1}{t}$dt$

$∴ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{1e}^{1}t^{2}\dfrac{1}{t}dt = ${\dfrac{t2}{2}}_{1e}^{1} = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2e^{2}}

and ${I}_{2} = {∫}_{1}^{e} \left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)x\log_{\mathrm{e}}x dx$

Let $\left(\dfrac{e}{x})x = t$

Taking natural logarithm on both sides, we get

$xln \left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right) =\ln t$

$⇒ x \left(1 - \ln x\right) = \ln t . . . . . . . . . \left(ii\right)$

$x$ $t$
$1$ $1\left(1 - \ln 1\right) = \ln t ⇒ t = e$
$e$ $e \left(1 - lne\right) = \ln t ⇒ t = 1$

Differentiating equation~\left(ii\right)$~both sides, we get

$⇒ $\l$left[x\left($0 - $\dfrac{1}{x}\right) + \left($1 - \ln x\right) . 1]dx = $\dfrac{dt}{t}~(using product rule of differentiation)

$⇒ \ln x = - $\dfrac{dt}{t}

$∴ {I}_{2} = {∫}_e^{1}t . $\dfrac{- dt}{t} = {- t}_e^{1} = \left(-$1\right) - \left(-$e\right) = e - 1$

Hence, required integral is ${I}_{1} - {I}_{2}$

$= \left(\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2e^{2}}\right) - \left(e - 1\right)$

$= \dfrac{3}{2} -e - \dfrac{1}{2e^{2}}.

questions.q: The value of $\alpha$ for which $4\alpha\mathop{∫}_{- 1}^{2}e^{- \alpha\left|x\right|}dx = 5$ , is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$4\alpha\left\{{∫}_{- 1}^{0}e^{\alphax}dx + {∫}_{0}^{2}e^{- \alphax}dx\right\} = 5$

$⇒ 4\alpha\left\{{\dfrac{e\alphax}{α}}_{- 1}^{0} + \dfrac{e- \alphax}{- \alpha}{}_{0}^{2}\right\} = 5$

$⇒ 4\alpha\left\{\left(\dfrac{1 - e^{- \alpha}}{α}\right) - \left(\dfrac{e^{- 2\alpha} - 1}{α}\right)\right\} = 5$

$⇒ 4\left(2 - e^{- \alpha} - e^{- 2\alpha}\right) = 5$

Put $e^{- \alpha} = t$

$⇒ 4t^{2} + 4t - 3 = 0 ⇒ \left(2t + 3\right)\left(2t - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ e^{- \alpha} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \alpha = \ln 2$

questions.q: Let $f$ be a real valued continuous function defined on the positive real axis such that $g(x)=\int_0^x \mathrm{t} f(\mathrm{t}) \mathrm{dt}$. If $\mathrm{g} \left($x^3\right)=x⁶+x⁷$, then value of $\sum_{r=1}^{15} f\left(\mathrm{r}^3\right) is :

questions.q: If the integral ${∫}_{0}^{10}\left[\sin 2\pix\right]e^{x - \left[x\right]}dx = \alphae^{- 1} + \betae^{- \dfrac{1}{2}} + \gamma,$~where $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are integers and  \left[x\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x,$~then the value of $\alpha + \beta + \gamma$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $I = {∫}_{0}^{10}\left[\sin 2\pix\right]e^{x - \left[x\right]}dx = {∫}_{0}^{10}\left[\sin 2\pix\right]e\left\{x\right\}dx,$~where~$x - \left[x\right] = \left\{x\right\}$~is the fractional part function.

We know that the \left\{x\right\}$~is a~periodic function with period~$1$~and also that~$\sin 2\pix$~is~a~periodic function with period~$\dfrac{2\pi}{2\pi} = 1 .$

Thus, the function $f\left(x\right) = \left[\sin 2\pix\right]e \left\{x\right\}$ is periodic with period $1 .$

If~f\left($x\right)$~is a periodic function with period~$T$~then~${∫}_{0}^{nT}f\left($x\right)dx = n{∫}_{0}^{T}f\left($x\right)dx, n \in N$

Therefore~$I = 10{∫}_{0}^{1}\left[$\sin 2\pix\right]e\left\{x\right\}dx$

$⇒ I = 10{∫}_{0}^{1} \left[\sin 2\pix\right]e^{x}dx$

Now, for~$0 ≤ x ≤ 1 ⇒ - 1 $\$lesin2\pix ≤ 1,$~hence~\left[$\sin 2x\right]$~can take values~$0$~and~$- 1$

$⇒ I = $10\left({∫}_{0}^{1 / 2} \left[$\sin 2\pix\right]e^{x}dx + {∫}_{1/2}^{1}\left[$\sin 2\pix\right]e^{x}dx\right)$

$⇒ I = 10 \left(0 + {∫}_{1/2}^{1}\dfrac{( -1 )}{ex}dx\right)$

$⇒ I = - 10{∫}_{1/2}^{1}e^{- x}dx$

$⇒ I = 10{e^{- x}}_{1/2}^{1}$

$⇒ I = 10 \left(e^{- 1} - e^{- 1 / 2}\right)$

Given,~$I = \alphae^{- 1} + \betae^{- $\dfrac{1}{2}} + \gamma,$~thus~$\alpha =10, \beta = -10, \gamma =0 .$

And,~$\alpha + \beta + \gamma =10 - 10 = 0 .$

$

questions.q: Let $\int_\alpha^{\log _e 4} \frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\sqrt{\mathrm{e}^x-1}}=\frac{\pi}{6}$. Then $\mathrm{e}^\alpha$ and $\mathrme^{-\alpha}$ are the roots of the equation :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int_\alpha^{\log 4} \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\sqrt{\mathrme^{\mathrm{x}}-1}}=\frac{\pi}{6} \\ & \text { Let } \mathrme^{\mathrm{x}}-1=\mathrm{t}^2 \\ & \mathrme^{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{dx}=2 \mathrm{t} \mathrm{dt} \\ & =\int \frac{2 \mathrm{dt}}{\mathrm{t}^2+1} \\ & =2 \tan ^{-1} \mathrm{t} \\ & =\left.2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\mathrme^{\mathrm{x}}-1}\right)\right|_\alpha ^{\log _{\mathrm{e}}^4} \\ & =2\left[\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{3}-\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\mathrm{e}^\alpha-1}\right]=\frac{\pi}{6} \\ & =\frac{\pi}{3}-\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\mathrm{e}^\alpha-1}=\frac{\pi}{12} \\ & \Rightarrow \tan ^{-1} \sqrt{\mathrm{e}^\alpha-1}=\frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \mathrm{e}^\alpha=2 \quad \mathrme^{-\alpha}=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \mathrm{x}^2-\left(2+\frac{1}{2}\right) \mathrm{x}+1=0 \\ & 2 \mathrm{x}^2-5 \mathrm{x}+2=0\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{- 1}^{1}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}\right)dx$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let

$I = {∫}_{- 1}^{1}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = 2{∫}_{0}^{1}\mathop{\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}\right) ⏟}_{I} \cdot \mathop{1 ⏟}_{II}dx$

$⇒ I = 2\left[{x\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}\right)}_{0}^{1} - {∫}_{0}^{1}x \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{1 + x}} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{1 - x}}\right)dx\right]$

$⇒ I = 2\log_{\mathrm{e}}\sqrt{2} - \dfrac{2}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\left\{\dfrac{x $\$left(\sqrt{1 - x} - \sqrt{1 + x}\rright)}{ \left(\sqrt{1 - x} + \sqrt{1 + x}\right)\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}\right\}$dx$

$⇒ I = $2\log_{\mathrm{e}}\sqrt{2} - {∫}_{0}^{1} \left\{\dfrac{x\left(\sqrt{1 - x} - \sqrt{1 + x}\right)2}{- 2x\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}\right\}dx$

$⇒ I = \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}$2\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2 - 2\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right)\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}dx$

$⇒ I = \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}$2\right) + {∫}_{0}^{1}$\$left(\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{1 - x^{2}}}{1 - x^{2}}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}$2\right) + {\sin^{- 1}x - x}_{0}^{1}$

$⇒ I = \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}$2\right) + \dfrac{π}{2} -1$

questions.q: $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{{∫}_{0}^{x}tsin\left(10t\right)dt}{x}$, is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& $I = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{{∫}_{0}^{x}tsin\left(10t\right)dt}{x}$

The given limiting form is the indeterminate form~$\dfrac{0}{0}$.

Thus, using~Newton-Leibnitz~Rule (differentiation under integral sign)~and L' Hospital Rule, we get,~

$I = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\dfrac{d}{dx}\left\{{∫}_{0}^{x}tsin\left(10t\right)dt\right\}}{\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x\right)}$

$= 0$.

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$~be continuous function satisfying $f\left(x\right) + f\left(x + k\right) = n$, for all $x \in R$~where $k > 0$~and $n$~is a positive integer. If ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{4nk}f\left(x\right)dx$~and~${I}_{2} = {∫}_{- k}^{3k}f\left(x\right)dx$, then
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,&

$f\left(x\right) + f\left(x + k\right) = n$~....(i)

Replacing~$x \to x + k$~in above equation we get,

$f\left(x + k\right) + f\left(x + 2k\right) = n$~.....(ii)

Subtraction equation (i) from equation (ii) we get,

$⇒ f \left(x\right) = f \left($x + 2k\right)$

$f \left(x\right)$~is periodic with period~$2k$

Now,~${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{4nk}f\left(x\right)dx = 2n{∫}_{0}^{2k}f\left(x\right)dx$

${I}_{2} = {∫}_{- k}^{3k}f\left(x\right)dx = 2{∫}_{0}^{2k}f\left(x\right)dx$

Now integrating both side of~$f\left(x\right) + f\left(x + k\right) = n$~with limit~${∫}_{0}^{k}$ we get,

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{k}f\left(x\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{k}f\left(x + k\right)dx = nk$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{k}f\left(x\right)dx + {∫}_k^{2k}f\left(x\right)dx = nk$

$⇒ {∫}_{0}^{2k}f\left(x\right)dx = nk$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2n^{2}k, {I}_{2} = 2nk$

$⇒ {I}_{1} + n{I}_{2} = 4n^{2}k$

$

questions.q: If the value of the integral ${∫}_{0}^{12}\dfrac{x2}{\left(1 - x^{2}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}}dx$~is~$\dfrac{k}{6}$, then~$k$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{k}{6} = {∫}_{0}^{12}\dfrac{x2}{\left(1 - x^{2}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}}dx$

Let~$x = sin\theta ⇒ dx = cos\thetad\theta$

$⇒ \dfrac{k}{6} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi6}\dfrac{\sin^{2}\theta}{\left(1 - \sin^{2}\theta\right)\dfrac{3}{2}}cos\thetad\theta ⇒ \dfrac{k}{6} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi6}\sin^{2}\theta\left(\cos^{3}\theta\right)cos\thetad\theta$

$⇒ \dfrac{k}{6} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi6}\tan^{2}\thetad\theta = {∫}_{0}^{\pi6}\left(sec^{2}\theta - 1\right)d\theta ⇒ \dfrac{k}{6} = {tan\theta - \theta}_{0}^{\pi6} = \left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{π}{6}\right) = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3} - \pi}{6}$

$⇒ k = 2\sqrt{3} - \pi$

questions.q: The value of ${∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}\left(2 + 3\sin x\right)\sin x\left(1 + \cos x\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Let,& $I = {∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}\dfrac{2 + 3\sin x}{\sin x\left(1 + \cos x\right)}dx$

Now rearranging the above integral we get,

$I = {∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}\dfrac{2}{\sin x\left(1 + \cos x\right)}dx + {∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}3\left(1 + \cos x\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}\dfrac{2\sin x}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + \cos x\right)}dx + {∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}3\left(2\cos^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right)dx$

$⇒ I = \mathop{{∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}\dfrac{2\sin x}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + \cos x\right)} d x ⏟}_{I1} + \dfrac{3}{2}\mathop{{∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}\sec^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) d x ⏟}_{I2}$

$⇒ I = \mathop{{∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}\dfrac{2\sin x}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + \cos x\right)}dx ⏟}_{I1} + \dfrac{3}{2} \times 2\mathop{{tan\dfrac{x}{2}}_{\pi3}^{\pi2} ⏟}_{I2}$

$⇒ I = \mathop{{∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}\dfrac{2\sin x}{\sin^{2}x \left(1 + \cos x\right)}dx ⏟}_{I1} + 3 \left($1 - $\dfrac{1}{3}\right)

Now solving~${I}_{1}$~we get,

${I}_{1} = {∫}_{\pi3}^{\$pi2}\d$dfrac{2\sin x}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + \cos x\right)}$dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2{∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}\d$dfrac{1}{\sin x\left(1 + \cos x\right)}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2{∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}\dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{2\tan \left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{1 + \tan^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}\right)\left(1 + \dfrac{1 - \tan \left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{1 + \tan^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}\right)}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{\pi3}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\left[1 + \tan^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]\sec^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{\tan \left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}dx$

Put~\tan \left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) =$v ⇒ $\dfrac{1}{2}\sec^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$dx = dv$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{1\ssqrt{3}}^{1}\dfrac{\left(1 + v^{2}\right)dv}{v}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(v\right) + $\d$dfrac{v2}{2}}_{1\sqrt{3}}^{1}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left($1\right) - \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) + \dfrac{1}{3}$

So,

$I = \dfrac{1}{3} + \log_{\mathrm{e}}\sqrt{3} + 3 \left($1 - $\dfrac{1}{3}\right)

$⇒ I = \dfrac{10}{3} - \sqrt{3} + \log_{\mathrm{e}}\sqrt{3}$

questions.q: The integral $\dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{\left(2 - x^{2}\right)dx}{\left(2 + x^{2}\right)\sqrt{4 + x^{4}}}$ is equal to ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $I = \dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{2 - x^{2}}{\left(2 + x^{2}\right)\left(\sqrt{4 + x^{4}}\right)}dx$

$= \dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{2 - x^{2}}{x^{2}\left(\dfrac{2}{x} + x\right)\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{4}{x^{2}} + x^{2}\right)}}dx$

$= \dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{\dfrac{2}{x^{2}} - 1}{\left(\dfrac{2}{x} + x\right)\sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{2}{x} + x\right)}^{2} - 4}}dx$

Now let $\dfrac{2}{x} + x = t, \left(- \dfrac{2}{x^{2}} + 1\right)dx = dt$

$I = - \dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{\infty}^{2\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{dt}{t\sqrt{t^{2} - 4}} = - \dfrac{12}{\pi}{∫}_{\infty}^{2\sqrt{2}}\dfrac{2tdt}{t^{2}\sqrt{t^{2} - 4}}$

Let $t^{2} - 4 = z^{2}, 2tdt = 2zdz$

$I = - \dfrac{12}{\pi}{∫}_{\infty}^{2}\dfrac{2zdz}{z\left(z^{2} + 4\right)} = - \dfrac{24}{\pi}{∫}_{\infty}^{2}\dfrac{dz}{\left(z^{2} + 4\right)} = - \dfrac{24}{\pi}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{z}{2}\right)}_{\infty}^{2}$

$= - \dfrac{24}{\pi}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 3$

questions.q: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function defined by $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{4x}{{4}^{x} + 2}$ and $M = \mathop{∫}_{f\left(a\right)}^{f\left(1 - a\right)}x\sin^{4}\left(x\left(1 - x\right)\right)dx$, $N = \mathop{∫}_{f\left(a\right)}^{f\left(1 - a\right)}\sin^{4}\left(x\left(1 - x\right)\right)dx; a \ne \dfrac{1}{2}$. If $\alphaM = \betaN, \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{N}$, then the least value of ${α}^{2} + {β}^{2}$ is equal to ______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{4x}{{4}^{x} + 2}$

$⇒ f\left(1 - x\right) = \dfrac{41 - x}{{4}^{1 - x} + 2}$

$⇒ f\left(1 - x\right) = \dfrac{4}{4 + 2 \cdot {4}^{x}} = \dfrac{2}{2 + {4}^{x}}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) + f\left(1 - x\right) = 1$

Now, solving $M = \mathop{∫}_{f\left(a\right)}^{f\left(1 - a\right)}x \cdot \sin^{4}\left(x\left(1 - x\right)\right)dx$

Now, using the formula ${∫}_a^{b}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_a^{b}f\left(a + b - x\right) d x$ we get,

$⇒ M = \mathop{∫}_{f\left(a\right)}^{f\left(1 - a\right)}\left(f\left(a\right) + f\left(1 - a\right) - x\right) \cdot \sin^{4}\left(f\left(a\right) + f\left(1 - a\right) - x\right)\left(1 - \left(f\left(a\right) + f\left(1 - a\right) - x\right)\right)dx$

$⇒ M = \mathop{∫}_{f\left(a\right)}^{f\left(1 - a\right)}\left(1 - x\right) \cdot \sin^{4}\left(\left(1 - x\right)x\right)dx$

$⇒ M = \mathop{∫}_{f\left(a\right)}^{f\left(1 - a\right)}\sin^{4}\left(\left(1 - x\right)x\right)dx - \mathop{∫}_{f\left(a\right)}^{f\left(1 - a\right)}x \cdot \sin^{4}\left(\left(1 - x\right)x\right)dx$

$⇒ M = N - M$

$⇒ 2M = N$

So, on comparing we get, $\alpha = 2, \beta = 1$

Hence, ${α}^{2} + {β}^{2} = {2}^{2} + {1}^{2} = 5$

Applying L'hospital rule, we get

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to 0} \left(\dfrac{12}{1 + x^{6}}\right)

$⇒ L = 12$

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ be a continuous function such that $f\left(x\right) + f\left(x + 1\right) = 2$ for all $x \in R$. If~${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{8}f\left(x\right)dx$ and ${I}_{2} = {∫}_{- 1}^{3}f\left(x\right)dx$, then the value of ${I}_{1} + 2{I}_{2}$ is equal to ________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) + f\left(x + 1\right) = 2$

Replace~$x\text{by}x + 1$

$f\left(x + 1\right) + f \left($x + 2\right) = 2$

By subtracting the equations, we get

$f \left($x\right) = f\left($x + 2\right)$

$⇒ f \left(x\right)$ is periodic with period $= 2$

${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{8}f\left(x\right)dx = 4{∫}_{0}^{2}f\left(x\right)dx$

$= 4{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(f\left(x\right) + f\left(1 + x\right)\right)dx = 8$

Similarly,~${I}_{2} = 2 \times 2 = 4$

Hence,~${I}_{1} + 2{I}_{2} = 16$

$
